html:
The Chilembwe uprising was a revolt in January 1915 in southern Nyasaland, led by John Chilembwe, a Baptist minister educated in the United States, against colonial rule.

Chilembwe ran an independent church and schools near Chiradzulu. He was angered by the harsh treatment of tenants on the nearby Magomero estate and by the recruitment of Africans to fight and carry loads for Britain in the First World War. His followers killed the estate manager and two other settlers.

The rising found little support and was crushed within days. Chilembwe was shot while fleeing, and dozens of followers were executed. He became a national hero of Malawi, on the banknotes and remembered on John Chilembwe Day, an early voice of the nationalism that Banda later led in Nyasaland.
sum: The Chilembwe uprising was a revolt in January 1915 in southern Nyasaland, led by John Chilembwe, a Baptist minister educated in the United States, against colonial rule.
